rule: GOAL: Fill the four middle slots with colors matching the top sequence from left to right. CONTROLS: Click a color token to select it, then click an empty slot to place it. RULE: The order of placement must strictly follow the color pattern shown at the top of the screen. TRAP: Assuming you can drag colors directly; you must select first, then place, or the action fails.

GOAL: Guide the character across the grid to the target location. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one tile per press, not sliding to walls. RULE: Each key press advances exactly one step, allowing precise pathing. TRAP: Assuming slide mechanics caused wasted moves; the character stops immediately after one tile.

GOAL: Clear the first stage using just two moves. CONTROLS: Arrows shifted the blue bar left or right; Space triggered the action. RULE: Aligning the bar under the falling block caught it, completing the level. TRAP: Overthinking complex beam reflection patterns wasted time, when simple alignment was the key.

GOAL: You needed to guide the plug to its target by shifting the surrounding walls. CONTROLS: Clicking the blue blocks moved the wall boundary, which pushed the plug along with it. RULE: The plug is stuck to the wall edge; it only moves when the wall moves under it. TRAP: Thinking the plug could move independently of the wall structure wasted time on direct clicks.

GOAL: Match five tiles to specific target colors using a hidden mapping. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the current tile’s cycle; select a tile to apply. RULE: Each tile cycles through colors independently; find the target color by rotating until it appears. TRAP: Assuming the rotation order was uniform across all tiles, wasting actions on blind guessing instead of probing each slot’s unique cycle.

GOAL: Move the square to the ball. CONTROLS: Click a dot to slide the square up to six units. RULE: The square slides to the nearest dot in that direction. TRAP: Clicking the ball directly does nothing; you must approach it via the rail.

GOAL: Push three crates onto marked spots. CONTROLS: Arrows move you; space pushes or pulls the crate you face. RULE: Crates slide until they hit a wall or another crate. TRAP: Pulling a crate often blocks its path; plan pushes so crates never touch walls prematurely.

GOAL: Slide the green plug right by eight units. CONTROLS: Click the bar to expand the middle band, which pushes the plug. RULE: Each click expands the band and moves the plug right by two. TRAP: Thinking the band would clamp at zero; it actually pushed further, clearing the level in just four clicks.

GOAL: Shrink the oversized cap by matching the die pattern, then slide it left into the handle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cap; clicks toggle grid cells to match the projected die pattern. RULE: Matching the die's pip layout consumes the pattern and halves the cap’s size, allowing passage through narrow channels. TRAP: Assuming the cap moves freely at its original size wastes time; you must shrink it first to fit the track.

GOAL: Match all seven grid cells to a shared target shape regardless of rotation. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; the UP button cycles the selected cell through shape variations. RULE: The puzzle checks for rotational equivalence, so any rotation of the correct shape counts as a win. TRAP: Assuming a fixed orientation or specific cycle position wasted time; rotating the view or cycling blindly was unnecessary.

GOAL: Turn all five switches on. CONTROLS: Click each switch to toggle it between dark and light. RULE: Every click flips the state of the single switch you hit. TRAP: Believing the pattern matched the yellow plug; ignore decorations and just light them all up.

GOAL: Match the grid’s starting white cells exactly. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; Enter toggles a cell’s color. RULE: The die shows the final count, not the shape; the starting layout is the true target. TRAP: Assuming the die’s pip pattern defined the required shape cost time trying to force a match to it.

GOAL: Match the top row's blue glyphs to the hidden words derived from the bottom yellow row. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP cycles the glyph choice for the current cell. RULE: Yellow row glyphs are rotated versions of the codebook entries, requiring rotation-aware matching. TRAP: Assuming segmentation lengths match the blue row count; the blue row length dictates the word count, not the yellow row.

GOAL: Transform a row of blue shapes into yellow shapes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; select matching source and target shapes to build the mapping. RULE: Apply two sequential transformations: first convert blue to pink, then pink to yellow. TRAP: Do not map blue directly to yellow; you must find the intermediate pink shape that links both steps in the chain.

GOAL: Move the square until it touches the ball. CONTROLS: Clicking a spot on the rail shifts the square that exact distance. RULE: Victory triggers when the square’s edge neighbors the ball, even diagonally. TRAP: Assuming you must land inside the ball wastes turns; adjacent contact is enough.

GOAL: Arrange colored blocks to match a hidden sequence revealed by feedback squares. CONTROLS: Click blocks to swap positions; press Space to verify the current arrangement. RULE: Feedback indicates how many leading positions in the target order match your layout. TRAP: Assuming all slots belong to one continuous row; separating distinct colored sections reveals the true reading order.

GOAL: Fill the first tank to the target line. CONTROLS: Left buttons push liquid to the neighbor on the left. RULE: A tank cannot hold more than its maximum capacity at any single moment. TRAP: You can move more liquid through a small tank than it holds by refilling it between transfers.

GOAL: Place seven colored tokens into gray slots to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click a palette token to select it, then click a slot to place it. Press space to confirm the solution. RULE: Read top slots left to right. When you pass a colored ring, fill that color’s box slots immediately before continuing. TRAP: Assuming slots fill strictly top to bottom ignores the ring triggers, causing invalid placements that waste moves.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens and a ring to match a hidden sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette items, then click slots to place them; press space to submit. RULE: The ring acts as a separator, splitting the reading order into two distinct groups. TRAP: Assuming slots read strictly left-to-right ignores how the ring breaks the flow, causing misaligned colors.

GOAL: Match the keypad pattern shown on the left selector to the right keypad, then activate the blue circle. CONTROLS: Click the left selector to choose an option, click right keypad bars to toggle them, and click the blue circle to submit. RULE: The right keypad must exactly mirror the dark bar pattern displayed for the selected option on the left device. TRAP: Assuming all bars should be dark or ignoring the specific pattern shown by the left selector leads to failed submissions.

GOAL: Place two blue rings adjacent in the red box while filling the rest with solid tokens. CONTROLS: Click tokens to select, click slots to place, press space to confirm the layout. RULE: The blue box sequence must repeat identically for each ring traversal, forcing adjacent ring placement. TRAP: Assuming rings must occupy separate boxes causes a mismatch; they must sit side-by-side in the red box.

GOAL: Fill four three-slot boxes to match a nine-color legend sequence. CONTROLS: Click rings to assign box destinations; click tokens to fill remaining slots. RULE: The first color in the legend dictates which ring goes into the central hub box first. TRAP: Assuming rings fill their own colored boxes; instead, they route the legend order to other boxes.

ESTABLISHED: The rod extends right from column 16. Objects R, N, and B block specific horizontal paths at different rows. FAILED: Extending right directly hits R, pushing B out of bounds. Moving R left without raising the head first leaves R in the upper path. GOAL IS NOT: Simply collecting items in order. You must clear the rod's horizontal lane completely before extending. CONTROLS: UP/DOWN moves the head vertically. LEFT/RIGHT extends or retracts the rod. Moving UP drags R; retracting drags N.

GOAL: Merge three small pieces into two larger shapes, then slide each shape to its matching target ball. CONTROLS: Clicking near a piece moves it toward the click if within range, but only if the move is legal. RULE: Two pieces of the same type merge into one when they land on the same spot, creating a bigger piece. TRAP: Assuming any click moves a piece. If a piece is too far or blocked, the click does nothing, wasting a turn.

GOAL: Fill three nested boxes with six tokens to match a hidden sequence. CONTROLS: Drag tokens to slots; press Space to submit. RULE: The middle box must contain a green ring to place the required yellow token at the center position. TRAP: Placing rings in the outer red box prevents the necessary nesting depth for the center match.

GOAL: Align codebook tiles so blue cells map correctly to pink examples. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor; UP cycles tile values. RULE: Cursor wraps right-to-left across all eight tiles in a fixed sequence. TRAP: Assuming fixed positions rather than wrapping navigation wasted moves searching for targets.

GOAL: Position two colored crosses so each covers its four matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross three units per press; Space submits the alignment. RULE: Each cross has vertical and horizontal arms; all four dots of a color must lie on these lines. TRAP: Assuming the cross moves one unit per press or that dots must touch only the arm tips.

GOAL: Guide two colored plugs so their red dots land exactly on the center of the plus markers. CONTROLS: Click the prong at the end of a plug to extend its body by three spaces. RULE: The red dot sits one space behind the tip, so extending the tip aligns the dot with the target. TRAP: Assuming the plug tip itself needed to touch the plus was wrong; only the trailing dot counts.

GOAL: Reach the far right side of the map without getting eaten by the red lunging monster. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character two spaces per press, sliding until you hit a wall or obstacle. RULE: The monster moves first at the start of each turn, lunging two spaces toward your current position. TRAP: Thinking you can dodge by moving sideways; the monster tracks your row, so you must break line of sight to survive.

GOAL: Collect scattered orange dots using a sliding X-shape. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece three spaces; Space switches between the X, diamond, and cross. RULE: Pieces slide a fixed distance per press, ignoring obstacles until they stop. TRAP: Assuming single-space movement caused excessive button presses and wasted the action budget.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the yellow tile aligns with the yellow brackets at the top-left. CONTROLS: Click the left arrow to rotate one way; click the right arrow to rotate the opposite way. RULE: The yellow brackets mark the target slot; only the yellow tile satisfies the win condition. TRAP: Clicking tiles directly does nothing; only the side arrows move the ring, so ignore direct tile clicks.

GOAL: Move the gray diamond into the target ring. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the white cross. Click the gray diamond to swap its position with the cross. RULE: The purple square always sits exactly halfway between the cross and the diamond, shifting as they move. TRAP: Thinking the white cross needed to enter the ring. The diamond is the correct piece to insert.

GOAL: Reduce all scattered pieces until only one remains on the board. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click the empty space behind an adjacent piece to jump. RULE: Jumping over a neighbor removes that neighbor and moves your piece to the empty spot beyond. TRAP: Trying to jump pieces that are not directly adjacent wastes turns; ensure a piece sits between you and the landing zone.

GOAL: Guide three agents to collect dots without colliding or exceeding the action limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active agent; Space cycles through agents. RULE: Only one agent moves per input, so plan paths to avoid blocking each other. TRAP: Assuming the bar is an action limit; it is actually a real-time timer that ticks between your moves.

GOAL: Make the active bottom-right grid match the small pattern shown in its center square. CONTROLS: Click individual tiles to toggle their color between red and blue. RULE: The center mini-grid reveals the exact target arrangement you must replicate in the main panel. TRAP: Assuming clicks affect neighboring tiles; they do not. Only the clicked tile changes.

GOAL: Match the big grid's red tiles to the mini grid's white tiles. CONTROLS: Click a big tile to toggle its color between blue and red. RULE: The mini grid shows the target pattern, where white cells equal red cells. TRAP: Assuming the mini grid was just a static display instead of a required target.

GOAL: Seat both blocks into their matching rings. CONTROLS: Click a block to activate it; arrows move the active block. RULE: Only the block with the white dot responds to arrow keys. TRAP: Assuming arrows move the visually nearest block rather than the specifically marked active one.

GOAL: Move both blocks to the top center notch. CONTROLS: Arrows moved blocks; they stuck together when touching. RULE: Blocks merge into one unit upon contact, moving as a pair. TRAP: Assuming merged blocks can separate or move independently again.

GOAL: Rearrange the grid into the target pattern using exactly eight moves. CONTROLS: Click buttons to rotate specific cycles of tiles clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Every move shifts tiles along a fixed loop, preserving the cycle's contents. TRAP: Believing moves affect all tiles equally; they only impact their specific loop.

GOAL: Cycle the glyph to the correct state before entering the box. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; covering the plus toggles the glyph. RULE: The box only opens when the glyph matches the target state. TRAP: Assuming the glyph state was irrelevant led to wasted movement and failed entries.

GOAL: Fill specific grid cells with orange tiles based on the mini-thumbnail patterns. CONTROLS: Click tiles to cycle their color until they match the required state. RULE: The center color of each thumbnail indicates which color the white cells in that pattern represent. TRAP: Assuming white always maps to the same color across levels, rather than matching the thumbnail's center.

GOAL: Guide two squares through a grid to reach the exit zone on the right side. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both squares simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Walls stop movement, but red hazard zones destroy any square that lands on them. TRAP: Assuming a blocked path is safe; moving into a hazard kills the square instantly.

GOAL: Cover dot clusters with matching color cursors to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plus cursor; Space switches between multiple cursors. RULE: A cursor must absorb a specific color from a source square before covering that color’s dots. TRAP: Assuming a single cursor could cover all colors or that color pickup was temporary.

GOAL: Move the cross so the purple square lands on the orange ring. CONTROLS: Click the cross to teleport it, or swap two objects to shift the square. RULE: The square centers on the average position of the gray and cross pieces. TRAP: Avoid placing the cross inside the ring's area, as it blocks the target.

GOAL: Color each cell to satisfy mini-clues where one color matches the center and another differs from it. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color through base, red, and orange. RULE: A clue’s white marker equals the center’s color; the gray marker is any color but the center’s. TRAP: Assuming gray meant a fixed specific color instead of just "not the center," which overcomplicated the logic.

GOAL: Align colored tiles within bracketed rings by rotating them. CONTROLS: Click left or right bracket buttons to spin the enclosed ring clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Each click shifts every tile in the ring one position along its circular path. TRAP: Assuming both buttons rotate in the same direction; they actually spin opposite ways.

GOAL: Seat four blocks into their matching ring holes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block; clicks select a new active block. RULE: Blocks slide until blocked, but can overlap ring outlines. TRAP: Assuming blocks stop at the first obstacle; they slide to the last free spot before stopping.

ESTABLISHED: White walls and red path are static. Red 3x3 object is unreachable. Gray blocks trail the player. FAILED: Moving walls, sliding blocks, pressing SPACE on red path, covering red trail, pushing red blob. GOAL IS NOT: Traversing the red path, pushing the red blob, or covering the red trail with gray blocks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move player. SPACE interacts but had no effect on red objects or walls. Gray blocks follow player path.

GOAL: Move the black shape to the mirrored position of the yellow target across the central divider. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the shape; left and right move horizontally, up and down move vertically. RULE: The puzzle solves when the black shape exactly overlaps the yellow target's mirrored location. TRAP: Assuming movement requires crossing the divider; simply moving toward the mirror position works without passing through.
GOAL: Fit the plug into the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug three steps. RULE: Align prongs with pins to connect. TRAP: Assuming you must stop short of the socket.

GOAL: Fill the final empty slot in the target bar. CONTROLS: Arrows move the snake; Space absorbs or deposits rings. RULE: A four-block ring snaps to the slot when the head aligns and Space is pressed. TRAP: Thinking the body blocks movement through the bar; it passes freely, allowing direct alignment.

GOAL: Align the yellow door with the yellow slot to open the path. CONTROLS: Top blue moves the wall right; bottom blue moves it left. RULE: The door fits only when its columns match the slot's columns exactly. TRAP: Ignoring the arrow's direction and moving the wall the wrong way wastes turns.

GOAL: Align the black block's reflection with the yellow target by positioning the mirror axis and the block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece three units; Space switches focus between the mirror axis and the block. RULE: The reflection mirrors across the axis, so moving the axis shifts the reflection twice as far as moving the block. TRAP: Forgetting to switch focus with Space before moving the axis causes block moves instead, wasting turns and misaligning the reflection.

GOAL: Guide the token from the start to the exit in the sliding maze. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push the token in that direction until it hits a wall. RULE: The token slides across open gray passages and stops only when blocked by black walls. TRAP: Believing you stop after one step; you must plan long slides to reach targets efficiently.

GOAL: Align the green door's rows with the slot's rows to pass through. CONTROLS: Blue buttons shift the door or walls vertically; two move the door, two adjust barriers. RULE: Success depends only on matching row coordinates; horizontal position is irrelevant. TRAP: Assuming walls must move to create space wastes clicks; only door alignment matters.

GOAL: Paint the mold's bottom band purple while keeping the top band white. CONTROLS: Arrows tilt and move the stamp; clicks pour paint; space rotates the stamp upright. RULE: The stamp paints only the cells it physically touches, so approach from below to hit just the bottom band. TRAP: Assuming paint fills from the top like a container, when the mold actually acts as a canvas stamped by the block.

GOAL: Position two shapes so they match their mirror images across a horizontal axis. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; spacebar switches between shapes. RULE: Shapes must land on target outlines, and their reflections must perfectly align with corresponding outlines on the other side of the axis. TRAP: Moving the second shape first causes a collision with the first shape’s starting position; always move the lower shape away before sliding the upper one.

ESTABLISHED: The green block sits below a four-by-four piece. The red plug connects to a lower section. FAILED: Moving the green block to touch the piece above it did not solve the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply making the green pin touch the block directly above it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green block. Clicking the red plug toggles its shape between two states.

GOAL: Place two mirrored pieces onto yellow targets using a movable axis. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece or axis. Space switches between axis and pieces. RULE: The axis reflects piece positions vertically, so aligning one piece automatically aligns its mirror. TRAP: Thinking the axis must stay away from pieces; it actually passes through them to create the reflection.

GOAL: Slide the green plug down and left to align its pins with the blue plug's prongs, then move the blue plug down and left to connect them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected plug; clicking a plug selects it for movement. RULE: Plugs connect when their pins and prongs occupy the same cells, even if they pass through other static obstacles. TRAP: Assuming movement is blocked by static cells; only walls and other movable plugs stop you, not the connection points themselves.

ESTABLISHED: Removing a block clears its 5x5 area and any black cells directly above it until water. FAILED: Removing blocks in the lower band did not clear the black row below them. GOAL IS NOT: Simply creating a channel from the water down to the current block layer. CONTROLS: Clicking removes a block. Arrow keys move the player.

GOAL: Lure the red enemy away from the upper path to reach the exit on the right. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: The enemy chases you along straight lines, so stepping into its column pulls it away from its guard post. TRAP: Believing the enemy is stationary wastes time; you must actively bait it to open the route.

GOAL: Guide the bubble to the pink cross marker. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the bubble horizontally and vertically. RULE: The bubble floats upward automatically; you must steer it into position. TRAP: Assuming the black box behind the cross is a solid wall, when it is merely the sprite's background.

GOAL: Move water between five bars to align three target levels, completing the puzzle in exactly 14 clicks. CONTROLS: Click bar sides to pour water; left clicks drain to the neighbor, right clicks fill from the neighbor. RULE: Water flows only until the source is empty or the destination is full, changing levels in fixed increments. TRAP: Assuming clicks always change levels; clicking a full destination or empty source wastes a move and stalls progress.

GOAL: Guide the green block to the yellow pin. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; clicking the red piece rotates the barrier. RULE: Rotations are safe if the block stands on the fixed base, not the rotating arm. TRAP: Believing the block must stand on the moving arm to pass through the rotating gate.

GOAL: Match seven unique glyphs to their corresponding bottom nodes. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows move the cursor between slots. Up and Down arrows cycle the selected glyph's shape. RULE: The top glyph must visually align with the bottom node's shape to clear the slot. TRAP: Assuming the glyph cycle order was sequential; it was a scrambled sequence, requiring careful mapping of the correct rotation path.

GOAL: Move blocks from the bottom tray to the top slots to match colors. CONTROLS: Click a block in the tray, then click the target slot to swap them. RULE: Only one block moves per turn; the displaced block drops into the clicked tray position. TRAP: Assuming slots accept multiple blocks or that tray positions stay static after a swap.

GOAL: Move the chain head upward to touch the top bubble. CONTROLS: Click any slot to move the head directly to that location. RULE: The head can only jump within a limited range, roughly three chain links away. TRAP: Assuming you can click distant targets; long jumps fail silently, wasting your action count.

GOAL: Position the platform to catch the falling block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the platform horizontally or vertically; Space drops the block. RULE: The block stays attached to the platform while it moves, releasing only when Space is pressed again. TRAP: Thinking you must drop the block first; moving the empty platform wastes time before the drop.

ESTABLISHED: Five switches sit below a checkerboard screen. A plug and socket are aligned in the middle. The timer bar is at the top. The ball remains fixed at the bottom. FAILED: Clicking switches does nothing. Attempting to align switches with the checkerboard pattern failed. The ball does not rise with progress. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the checkerboard pattern. Making the ball rise. Aligning switches to screen columns. CONTROLS: Clicking switches produces no visible change.

GOAL: Drive the green plug’s pin exactly onto the cross’s center point. CONTROLS: The right green glyph extends the plug three cells per click. RULE: Contact with the cross only registers as success when the pin aligns perfectly with the center. TRAP: Stopping the plug when its tip touches the cross’s outer arm leaves the pin misaligned and fails the level.

GOAL: Align each colored cross so its arms cover all matching dots on the board. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross in fixed steps; spacebar switches to the next cross. RULE: A cross solves its color when its horizontal and vertical arms intersect the dots, requiring precise center alignment. TRAP: Believing arm tips must land exactly on dots wastes time; only the crossing point needs to align with the dot's row and column.

GOAL: Merge two snakes to create a larger head that overlaps the target bubble. CONTROLS: Clicking a grid cell moves the active snake head up to six steps in that direction. RULE: When two heads land within five cells of each other, they merge into a single larger snake. TRAP: Moving a snake directly to the bubble fails if it is too small; you must merge with another snake first to reach the target.

GOAL: Connect the blue block to the wire without moving it. CONTROLS: Left retracts the wire, pulling connected blocks along. Up moves the wire vertically. Right extends the wire tip. RULE: Extending the wire into a stationary block connects it without pushing, if the block is already aligned. TRAP: Moving the wire up first pushes the blue block out of alignment, making it unreachable by a simple extension.

GOAL: Locate the hidden center of a fragmented X shape by analyzing scattered pixel coordinates. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to navigate the interface and submit the calculated central point of the diagonal lines. RULE: The intersection point is defined by the most frequent differences and sums of row and column indices among connected diagonal pixels. TRAP: Treating isolated decorative dots as part of the main diagonal arms, which skews the statistical mode calculation.

ESTROLISHED: A 3x3 grid of green cells and a directional tip exist. A surge occurs when green cells match a specific plus pattern. FAILED: Clicking cells to form the plus pattern via white states did not clear the level within the action budget. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the plus pattern with the current tip orientation or state alone. CONTROLS: Clicking cells cycles colors. Arrow keys rotate the tip.

GOAL: Clear the level by merging three separate heads into one large entity. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the nearest head one step toward the cursor. RULE: Heads only react if the click is within a specific distance, with the closest head claiming the move. TRAP: Assuming ties are safe; nearly equidistant heads caused hesitation, wasting time calculating precise offsets to ensure a clear winner.

GOAL: Shrink the plug tip to a nub and slide it left through the narrow channel to connect with the head. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug tip. Clicking keypad cells toggles colors to match the socket's pin pattern. RULE: Matching the pin pattern exactly triggers a surge that shrinks the tip, allowing passage through the thin arm section. TRAP: Moving the wide tip directly left fails because it is too large to fit into the narrow connection channel.

GOAL: Align the block with the ring center to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Clicking an end swaps it with the cursor; the block always stays at the wire's midpoint. RULE: The block position is determined by the average of the two wire endpoints. TRAP: Assuming you can drag the block directly; you must instead move the endpoints to shift the midpoint.

GOAL: Align the tip with the head and push it inside to win. CONTROLS: Click keypad cells to trigger a surge that lifts the tip; use arrow keys to move it. RULE: A surge instantly relocates the tip upward, bypassing the need to climb manually through narrow passages. TRAP: Assuming the tip must shrink to a nub to enter the head; it fits at full size once aligned.

GOAL: Align three shapes to cover all dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: Shapes cover dots only when their outlines align perfectly with dot positions. TRAP: Assuming the center dot is part of the outline; hollow shapes do not cover their own center point.

GOAL: Place the plug onto the cross to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug one grid step in that direction. RULE: The plug must fully cover the cross symbol to trigger success. TRAP: Assuming a straight vertical path works; walls block direct routes, forcing a detour.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align the red and green plugs with their matching sockets. CONTROLS: Click a ring segment to rotate it clockwise; click plugs to adjust their orientation. RULE: Each plug must face the center of the ring to make a connection. TRAP: Thinking the yellow bracket was a fixed marker; it actually moves to the next active segment after every rotation.

GOAL: Move all pieces into the center so their average position lands exactly on the target spot. CONTROLS: Click a piece to slide it until it hits a wall or another piece. RULE: The game calculates the final center by averaging the last position of every piece, then rounding down. TRAP: Believing pieces can stop anywhere. They slide fully, so you must use other pieces as temporary walls to adjust the average.

GOAL: Guide the crosses to merge into a single group at the target spot. CONTROLS: Click a cross to select it, then click the highlighted destination to move it. RULE: When crosses land on the same cell, they combine into one larger piece. TRAP: Do not assume moves are independent; overlapping causes merging, which reduces your total count.

GOAL: Place the plus and X shapes so their arms touch the target dots. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected shape; Space switched between them. RULE: Only the tip of a shape’s arm could paint a dot, not its center. TRAP: Assuming the plus’s long bar would paint distant dots, when only the center or tips actually touched targets.

GOAL: Place two yellow tokens onto specific bracket slots by sliding them along horizontal and vertical tracks. CONTROLS: Six plugs shift entire rows or columns: red moves left or up, green moves right or down. RULE: Moves are global permutations, so tokens never collide; you only need to align each token to its target row and column. TRAP: Assuming plugs only move single tiles wastes time; they actually shift the entire track, requiring you to plan for whole-row shifts.

ESTABLISHED: Two blue squares start at spiral ends. Top band spans cols 19-49. Squares move on a grid with 5-col steps. FAILED: Moving squares to top center (cols 24/34) did not clear level. Pressing SPACE did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing squares adjacent at the spiral's top center. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move squares. SPACE does nothing.

GOAL: Route two separate chains to their target rings without overlapping paths. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the active end; click a chain end to switch control to that chain. RULE: The block always stays centered exactly between the two ends of its chain. TRAP: Assuming you can move both ends simultaneously; you must alternate control between chains to position them correctly.

GOAL: Match the grid’s colors to the plug’s pattern to complete the puzzle. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle their color between red and blue. RULE: Each plug’s arms and corners map directly to the eight surrounding grid cells. TRAP: Assuming the plug reflects the current state rather than the required target pattern.

GOAL: Make all panel cells orange to match the plug shapes. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color between blue and orange. RULE: Each plug defines the required color for its specific cells, with overlaps requiring both conditions. TRAP: Assuming plugs are live indicators rather than fixed targets caused unnecessary probing and confusion.

GOAL: Swap the yellow and orange tokens between their starting positions on the interlocking rings. CONTROLS: Rotate the left ring clockwise or counter-clockwise; rotate the right ring clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: A token transfers between rings only when standing on a shared intersection cell during a rotation. TRAP: Assuming tokens can jump rings anywhere; they are locked to their current ring unless at a specific bridge point.

ESTABLISHED: Orange pushes the sky column right, then up through the pocket. Yellow and green rise together as a cluster. FAILED: Moving the column without extending orange first; growing yellow before clearing the path. GOAL IS NOT: Placing the sky piece in the initial pocket or moving green independently. CONTROLS: Drag to extend orange. Drag yellow to pull green. Drag column to shift position.

GOAL: Turn specific red cells orange to satisfy the puzzle's color constraints. CONTROLS: Click cells to change their color from red to orange. RULE: A white block on a plug indicates that its adjacent cell must match the plug's center color. TRAP: Thinking gray blocks imposed a strict color requirement; they actually just meant no constraint applied.

GOAL: Pinch the arch's bottom slit by moving the two squares to its immediate left and right edges. CONTROLS: Arrows slide squares; Space locks them in place; Clicks trigger actions or reset. RULE: The level clears only when the squares physically block the gap, not just when they touch. TRAP: Believing Space welds adjacent squares; it does nothing unless they are correctly aligned with the target zone.

GOAL: Align colored markers to match the target pattern across the grid. CONTROLS: Top and bottom buttons rotate the vertical loop; left and right buttons rotate the horizontal loop. RULE: The loops intersect at a shared center, so rotating one axis affects the position of markers on the other. TRAP: Treating the axes as independent puzzles wastes time; you must solve them simultaneously by checking the center alignment.

GOAL: Match hidden grid colors to visible clues using a three-color cycle. CONTROLS: Click a cell to rotate its color through blue, red, and orange. RULE: White marks force a specific color; gray marks forbid a color, leaving one valid option. TRAP: Assuming gray means "red" costs extra clicks; it only excludes the marked color, so choose the remaining valid hue.

ESTABLISHED: The left ring is reachable. Placing a plug inside the left ring's interior did not trigger a win. The right ring is currently inaccessible due to a purple wall blocking the path. FAILED: Simply covering the left ring's center with a plug. Moving the second plug near the wall without penetrating it. GOAL IS NOT: Just placing a single plug in any ring interior. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active plug. Space pushes adjacent objects. Budget decreases per move; running out resets the level.

ESTABLISHED: Blue plug moves freely on black paths, leaving gray trails. Red 3x3 block is solid. Blue ring at (7,5) is a socket. FAILED: Pressing SPACE at home or current location does nothing. Assuming red block is merely a passive obstacle. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the blue ring without resolving the red block's state. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug. SPACE attempts interaction, currently ineffective on open floor or home.

GOAL: Move the green dot to the top-left corner to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the dot; clicks toggle the blue wire between solid and checkerboard. RULE: The dot can only exit upward if the wire is checkerboard and aligned. TRAP: Assuming solid wires were passable wasted time trying to move through them.

GOAL: The puzzle asks you to align two shapes by moving them across the grid. CONTROLS: Press Down to shift pieces vertically and Left to shift them horizontally. RULE: Each move shifts the active piece exactly three spaces in the chosen direction. TRAP: Do not assume the pieces move one space at a time; this miscounting causes overshooting.

GOAL: Align the green plug's arms with the red socket pins. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug one space. RULE: The plug must slide directly into the socket to connect. TRAP: Avoiding overlap by stopping adjacent fails; tips must land exactly on the pins.

GOAL: Place two yellow tokens into the two marked corners at the top of the board. CONTROLS: Top buttons rotate the upper row; middle buttons shift the long snake-like path below. RULE: The top row is part of the main path, so shifting the snake moves the corners too. TRAP: Thinking the top row is separate from the main loop; ignoring this link wastes many turns.

GOAL: Slide the black piece down and shift the mirror left to match the target silhouette. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space switches control between the piece and the mirror. RULE: Only the object with white dots responds to arrow keys; the other stays still. TRAP: Moving the piece while the mirror is active wastes turns and solves nothing.

GOAL: Fill both empty sockets to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; clicks select a piece. RULE: Clicking a piece selects it, overriding the previous selection. TRAP: Assuming the original piece remains selected after clicking a new one.

GOAL: Align the yellow plug with the gap in the black bar to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click the upper blue block to shift the top wall left; click the lower blue block to shift the bottom wall right. RULE: The plug moves rigidly with the bottom gray section, while the gap moves independently in the top section. TRAP: Assuming the gray area is a single rigid body; it actually shears, moving top and bottom halves in opposite directions.

GOAL: Flip specific grid cells to match the target pattern within a tight action limit. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles it and its four orthogonal neighbors. RULE: A cell is toggled if it or any adjacent cell is clicked; the effect is symmetric. TRAP: Assuming the toggle matrix is symmetric by default; failing to account for non-checker cells receiving toggles from adjacent checkers caused invalid solutions.

GOAL: Guide a plug to a distant socket, requiring a specific push to clear the path. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; pressing away from it pushes the tail to open blocked corridors. RULE: The tail acts as a movable block; positioning it correctly is the only way to unblock the route. TRAP: Assuming the plug moves independently ignores that the tail must be pushed into place to clear obstacles.

GOAL: Move the dot to the yellow target using the rotating arm. CONTROLS: Arrows move the dot; clicking the plug rotates the red arm around its central pivot. RULE: Only the colored arm rotates; the gray socket remains fixed in place. TRAP: Believing the gray cap rotates with the arm, causing you to plan a path that leaves a gap.

GOAL: Move the green block into the gap by aligning it with the opening in the wall. CONTROLS: Clicking below the upper bar shifts the middle wall right and the upper wall left. Clicking below the lower bar shifts the lower wall right and the middle wall left. RULE: The walls are linked; moving one bar forces two walls to move in opposite directions simultaneously. TRAP: Believing the middle wall acts independently or that you can move only one wall at a time.

GOAL: Guide the plug to collect three rings and drop them into matching slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; the plug faces its last direction. Space attaches a ring from the facing block or drops a held one. RULE: Carrying a ring locks the plug’s orientation; it only reorients when empty. TRAP: Assuming movement always turns the cap. While carrying, the plug slides straight without rotating, causing missed attachments.

GOAL: Align solid shapes with ghost outlines and position reflections above targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move active piece or mirror; Space cycles selection. RULE: Reflections are vertical mirrors of pieces across the central line. TRAP: Moving the mirror shifts all reflections simultaneously, requiring precise coordinate math.

ESTABLISHED: Three rooms connect vertically. Two blocks in the middle room's ceiling have been removed, opening a path upward. FAILED: Clicking blocks on the left side did not connect to the top room due to a black barrier. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the isolated left-side blocks or assuming the top room is fully accessible from below yet. CONTROLS: Clicking a block clears a seven-row by five-column area centered on the click.

GOAL: Guide the plug from start to finish by navigating a grid where movement logic depends on parity. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug exactly two cells in the chosen direction, provided the intermediate cell is passable. RULE: The plug only occupies cells where the row and column indices sum to an even number, effectively jumping over odd cells. TRAP: Assuming you can move one cell to adjust position; this breaks parity and prevents reaching the goal.

ESTABLISHED: The container holds purple goo. The target requires the bottom half purple and top half white. Pouring purple fills the lower section, but a white triangle gap remains at the bottom center. FAILED: Tipping the container left or right before pouring did not eliminate the white triangle gap or align the fill correctly. GOAL IS NOT: Simply filling the entire block with one color or leaving the container upright during the final pour. CONTROLS: Arrow keys tip the container to change the pour angle. Selecting a color changes the fluid type. The spacebar executes the pour action.

GOAL: Align the mirror band and two pieces to complete the reflection circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected object; spacebar cycled selection between the mirror and pieces. RULE: Objects pass through the mirror band freely, allowing vertical movement across its zone. TRAP: Believing the mirror must move last to avoid collision; moving it first cleared the path for the pieces.

GOAL: Move the green piece into the yellow piece’s empty slots. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the green piece down eight times, then left four times. One click confirmed the move. RULE: Pieces must slide freely without overlapping other shapes or pins to reach the target. TRAP: Assuming the green piece could pass through the yellow body. It blocked the path, forcing a precise detour around it.

GOAL: Move the block up the diagonal trail to reach the socket. CONTROLS: Click a dot to jump the block toward it; dots shift down to fill the gap. RULE: The block can only jump a limited distance, so use short hops. TRAP: Trying to jump directly to a distant dot fails and wastes time.

GOAL: Paint the block’s top half white and bottom half purple to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click cartridges to select colors; Space pours the selected color from the current container position. RULE: The container’s tilt determines which half of the block receives the paint. TRAP: Assuming every region needs a fresh pour; once the block is fully purple, only the final white pour is needed.

GOAL: Clear the board by removing all colored blocks. CONTROLS: Click a block to remove it; remaining blocks fall down to fill gaps. RULE: Blocks must be removed in groups of two or more adjacent same-colored tiles. TRAP: Assuming single isolated blocks can be clicked; they cannot be removed and may block other moves if ignored.

GOAL: Descend the plug five cells by closing all circuits. CONTROLS: Click switches to toggle prongs; click the plug to run. RULE: A switch conducts current only when both prongs are black. TRAP: Assuming single black prongs conduct power wastes actions on incomplete circuits.

GOAL: Move the plug to the target without touching the spark. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; the spark strikes only along its marked line. RULE: The spark hits only cells directly in its facing path, not adjacent ones. TRAP: Assuming the spark strikes all nearby tiles or blocks entry from any side.

GOAL: Reach the pink cross at the top of the upper room. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; clicking a block removes it to open a path. RULE: Removing the overhead block lets the player float up into the higher water chamber. TRAP: Believing the cross is unreachable without first clearing the ceiling block above your starting position.

GOAL: Guide the fluid into a specific socket gap without letting it spill onto the ground or fill the wrong area. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue deflector bar; the spacebar releases the fluid from the plug. RULE: Fluid spreads across the top of any surface it lands on before falling off the edges. TRAP: Assuming the fluid pours straight down like a laser; it actually flows laterally over obstacles, requiring precise bar placement to direct the fall.

GOAL: Guide the plug to the designated node within the strict action limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug one cell at a time across the grid. RULE: Only specific colored nodes act as valid starting points and destinations. TRAP: Assuming the grid dimensions are uniform causes errors when the play area shrinks or changes shape.

GOAL: Fill the box slots to match the top pattern. CONTROLS: Click a color to select it, then click an empty slot to place it. RULE: Placing a color swaps the large colored block with the small gray placeholder. TRAP: Thinking you could click slots directly; you must select the color first.

GOAL: Match each bottom tile to its legend partner by rotating the top row. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor between columns; Up and Down rotate the tile under the cursor. RULE: Each bottom tile must align with the specific top tile connected to it by a gray bar in the legend. TRAP: Believing tiles could be swapped between columns rather than just rotated in place.

GOAL: Guide fluid streams into the three upper notches. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it; use arrow keys to move; space to release fluid. RULE: Bars only block fluid if the stream lands directly on top of them; passing alongside is safe. TRAP: Assuming adjacent bars deflect fluid sideways; they do not, allowing streams to pass freely next to them.

GOAL: Transform the grid by eliminating all white squares to reach the final state. CONTROLS: Click to select specific cells and press Space to trigger the transformation mechanic. RULE: Selected white cells flash and convert to gray only when the correct spatial pattern is formed. TRAP: Including static corner brackets in your selection merges distinct clusters, obscuring the true target shapes and wasting moves.

GOAL: Extend colored plugs to touch cross arms. CONTROLS: Click glyphs to grow or shrink plugs. RULE: Plugs change size by three rows per click. TRAP: Thinking you must stop exactly at the arm row; overshooting to cover the whole cross also works.

GOAL: Align the selected cross center over the target dot. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the cross three cells; Space switches which cross is active. RULE: Movement is strict three-cell jumps that halt completely at the board edge. TRAP: Assuming a press moves one cell wastes actions; you must account for the three-cell stride and edge clipping.

GOAL: Rotate seven glyphs to match hidden target shapes using loop positions. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor; UP/DOWN cycles glyph rotation; left/right shifts position. RULE: Each slot has a unique target shape from the legend, checked by visual match. TRAP: Assuming all slots cycle identically; rotation direction or offset varies per slot, causing misalignment.

GOAL: Connect the plug to the blue socket by routing the cord through obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug or extend/retract the cord tip. RULE: The moving tip pushes any colored block it hits sideways, clearing a path. TRAP: Believing blocks are static; failing to use the tip to shove the green block left first blocks access to the blue socket.

GOAL: Transform the yellow sequence into the matching blue sequence using shape rules. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; Up cycles through shapes at the current blue slot. RULE: Each yellow chunk maps to a specific blue shape; the total blue length must match the sum of mapped outputs. TRAP: Assuming yellow slots are editable; only blue slots can be changed, so focus solely on fixing the blue strip.

GOAL: Fill slots with colored cartridges in a specific sequence. CONTROLS: Click a cartridge to select it, then click a slot to place it; press Space to submit or check hints. RULE: Follow the depth-first order of the structure, filling sub-containers before moving to the next main slot. TRAP: Assuming slots are filled strictly left-to-right, ignoring nested sub-boxes that interrupt the linear flow.

GOAL: Move all bars to the bottom row without overlapping. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it, then use arrow keys to slide it and space to confirm. RULE: Only the selected bar moves; clicking another bar deselects the current one. TRAP: Trying to move a bar that is not currently active results in no action.

GOAL: Place cartridges into red and green boxes, using a ring as a bridge. CONTROLS: Click items to select, click slots to place, press Space to reveal the next move. RULE: The green ring is a portable connector; it must be placed in the red box to unlock the green box. TRAP: Assuming the ring is fixed scenery. It is a movable part essential for accessing the second container.

GOAL: Clear Level 2 by guiding colored crosses to collect matching dots using only twelve directional moves and one selection switch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the active cross; spacebar cycled selection between orange, red, and blue markers. RULE: A cross only consumes dots of its own color, requiring precise routing to avoid blocking paths with other markers. TRAP: Assuming all dots were cleared prematurely; ignoring color matching led to wasted moves trying to collect incompatible items.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking the panel turns keypad diamonds white; clicking the head flashes all cells red. FAILED: Clicking the tip, keypad borders, panel borders, and background produced no visible change. GOAL IS NOT: A single successful click sequence ending immediately, nor a simple pattern reproduction matching the initial four cells. CONTROLS: Panel click resets keypad state; head click triggers error; other clicks are inert; actions deplete a shared bar.

GOAL: Connect the head to the gray diamond to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click any grid cell to move the head; the cord trails behind. RULE: The head must land exactly on the diamond's center to win. TRAP: Thinking the cord needed to pass through the ring; only the head's final position matters.

GOAL: Guide the plug to the socket by first collecting the key hidden behind the wall. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug one step; the orange tip must reach the blue glyph. RULE: The socket door only opens after the plug passes through the cross to collect the key. TRAP: Thinking covering the cross completes the level; it merely unlocks the path to the true exit.

GOAL: Arrange the ring’s colors to match the fixed bracket’s target sequence. CONTROLS: Clicking a plug rotates the entire ring one step toward that plug. RULE: Each click shifts every slot to the adjacent position, preserving relative order. TRAP: Clicking a specific block does not move just that block; the whole ring shifts.

GOAL: Reduce scattered crosses to a single survivor by jumping over neighbors. CONTROLS: Click a cross to select it, then click the landing spot beyond the piece you jump. RULE: Each jump removes the crossed piece and moves your cross to the empty space behind it. TRAP: Assuming isolated pieces are dead ends; creating adjacent pairs through careful jumps unlocks chain reactions.
